UnitStatement: The validation/benchmarks/nonlinear crate provides original nonlinear support regression benchmarks for OpenPipeStress.

Nonlinear benchmark fixtures use invented values and direct calls into committed nonlinear-support and solver-diagnostics APIs; they are software regression checks only with no protected standards content, real project values, external commercial outputs, or authority claims.
CANONICAL_DIMENSIONS enumerates the allowed dimension identifiers (e.g., length, force, moment, pressure, stress, area, second_moment_area, section_modulus) plus a TBD sentinel.
Enum NonlinearRegressionFamily classifies fixtures into ActiveSet, Gap, LiftOff, Friction, and NonConvergence families.
Enum RedistributionStatus has the single variant PublicOriginal.
Enum ReviewDisposition has the single variant AcceptedInventedFixture.
Struct BenchmarkProvenance records source_name, source_location, source_license, contributor, contributor_assertion, redistribution_status, and review_disposition for a fixture.

BenchmarkProvenance::public_original builds provenance asserting content was generated from invented support states and not copied from protected standards, commercial software examples, proprietary data, private data, or real project records.

BenchmarkProvenance::is_publicly_usable requires PublicOriginal redistribution, AcceptedInventedFixture disposition, non-empty source fields, and contributor_assertion containing the not-copied and invented-support-states phrases.
BenchmarkProvenance::source_artifact_exists verifies the provenance source_location resolves to a file under the repo root.
Struct FixtureUnitBasis records explicit fixture-local units for displacement, translational/rotational reaction, friction coefficient, and residual tolerance, with a note field.

FixtureUnitBasis::is_explicit_fixture_basis requires the PKG09 nonlinear unit-system ref, fixture-local-explicit-units-no-conversions status, non-empty unit fields, dimensionless residual tolerance, and a note stating the unit catalog remains TBD.

NONLINEAR_FIXTURE_UNIT_BASIS encodes explicit fixture-local units: displacement mm, translational reaction N, rotational reaction N-m, friction coefficient ratio, residual tolerance count/dimensionless, with project unit catalog remaining TBD and no conversion constants.
Struct DimensionedObservation records a named value with unit, dimension, and optional tolerance_policy.
Struct ExpectedState pairs a support_id with an expected ActiveSetState.
Struct ExpectedDiagnostic records an expected SolverDiagnosticCode, DiagnosticSeverity, and SolverStatus.

Struct NonlinearRegressionCase bundles a fixture id, family, description, assumptions, provenance, unit basis, active-set iteration input, expected states/changed-supports/residual-norm/converged flag, optional expected diagnostic, and observations.
NonlinearRegressionCase::run evaluates the active-set iteration for the case input via evaluate_active_set_iteration.
NonlinearRegressionCase::expected_report builds a SolverDiagnosticReport using the expected status (defaulting to MechanicsSolved) and the diagnostics from the run.
NonlinearRegressionCase::tolerance_policy_is_unresolved holds when every observation has no tolerance_policy.
NonlinearRegressionCase::has_dimensioned_observations requires every observation value finite, units non-empty, dimension in CANONICAL_DIMENSIONS, and an explicit fixture unit basis.
NonlinearRegressionCase::matches_expected_outcome compares the run's states, changed supports, residual norm, converged flag, and diagnostic against the expected values.
fixture_inventory returns the five nonlinear regression cases: active-set one-way, gap closure, lift-off, friction transition, and unresolved non-convergence.
missing_required_families returns any of the five required nonlinear families not represented in the supplied fixtures.

Fixture active_set_one_way_fixture: an invented one-way support activates from a positive trial reaction; expected state Active, residual norm 1.0, not converged, with a NonConvergence warning diagnostic.
Fixture gap_closure_fixture: an invented positive-clearance gap (0.25 mm) remains closed at its explicit clearance; expected state Active, no changed supports, residual 0.0, converged, no diagnostic.

Fixture lift_off_fixture: an invented lift-off support loses contact when the trial reaction reaches zero; expected state Inactive, residual 1.0, not converged, with a NonConvergence warning diagnostic.
Fixture friction_transition_fixture: an invented friction pair (coefficient 0.30) classifies one support as sticking and one as sliding; expected residual 0.0, converged, no diagnostic.
Friction limit is coefficient times positive normal reaction; the case uses invented normal and tangential reactions with no component catalog data.

Fixture unresolved_nonconvergence_fixture: an invented support remains changed at the configured iteration limit (4); expected state Active, residual 1.0, not converged, with a NonConvergence failure diagnostic and SolveFailed status.
Helper diagnostic_matches checks that absence of expected diagnostic implies empty diagnostics, otherwise that exactly one diagnostic matches the expected code and severity.
Test inventory_covers_required_nonlinear_families asserts the inventory has no missing required families and contains exactly five fixtures.
Test fixtures_are_public_original_and_unit_aware asserts each fixture is publicly usable, its provenance source artifact exists, has dimensioned observations, and unresolved tolerance policy.
Test active_set_gap_lift_off_and_friction_outcomes_are_deterministic asserts every fixture matches its expected outcome.
Test nonconvergence_fixture_reports_failure_diagnostic asserts the case does not converge, is blocked, and reports one NonConvergence failure diagnostic mentioning non-convergence after 4 iterations.
Test expected_reports_preserve_warning_and_failure_statuses asserts the active-set warning report is SolvedWithWarnings (not blocked) and the non-convergence report is SolveFailed (blocked).
Cargo package open_pipe_stress_stress_benchmarks (v0.1.0, edition 2021, publish=false) provides original stress recovery verification benchmarks for OpenPipeStress.
The stress benchmarks crate depends on frame_kernel, stress_recovery, and straight_pipe core crates by path.
The validation/benchmarks/stress crate contains original stress recovery verification fixtures for DEL-09-02, the stress recovery benchmark suite.

Stress fixtures are public project content because inputs, expected values, and derivations come from elementary open mechanics, not copied from protected standards examples, code formulas, commercial benchmarks, proprietary values, allowables, SIF/flexibility factors, or code-specific acceptance criteria.

Stress numerical comparison values are regression evidence for current code-neutral stress recovery behavior; release thresholds, tolerance policy, CI gate policy, stress range acceptance, fatigue criteria, and professional reliance remain TBD.

Stress fixture values carry explicit unit identifiers under PKG09-STRESS-FIXTURE-UNITS-EXPLICIT-N-M-PA, a fixture-local basis only that does not define project conversion constants or the canonical unit catalog (TBD).

The stress crate records readiness metadata; final tolerance policy, release thresholds, CI gate policy, result-envelope/export integration, benchmark publication scope, canonical unit/conversion policy, and professional reliance remain TBD.

Rust tests assert every stress fixture has public-original provenance, fixture-local units, dimensioned expected values, unresolved tolerance policy, and that the READMEs list the current fixture inventory.

The stress benchmark fixture families span axial-normal, bending-normal, torsional-shear, pressure-membrane, stress-range, integrated straight-pipe, load-to-resultant, oriented load-to-stress, partial-span, station-sweep, thermal axial-effect, combined axial-bending, and canonical analytical resultant stress.

The mechanics hand-calculation notes support DEL-09-01, the mechanics benchmark suite.

All mechanics hand-calc numeric values are invented for public verification fixtures derived from elementary open mechanics; they are not protected standards, commercial examples, proprietary values, code-specific acceptance criteria, or professional approval evidence.
For mechanics hand-calcs, final tolerance policy, release thresholds, CI gate policy, benchmark publication scope, external validation claims, and professional reliance remain TBD.

Mechanics hand-calc notes use explicit fixture-local unit identifiers mapping quantity families to units and canonical dimensions (e.g., length m, force N, moment N-m, stress Pa, second moment of area m^4, section modulus m^3, linear stiffness N/m).
The project unit catalog and conversion constants remain TBD for the mechanics hand-calc notes.
The mechanics benchmark crate source inventory is mirrored in the README so each fixture has an explicit public-original hand-calculation note.
The mechanics fixture inventory maps fixture IDs to their hand-calculation note files (e.g., MECH-CANTILEVER-TIP-FORCE to cantilever_tip_force.md).
MECH-CANTILEVER-TIP-FORCE: cantilever benchmark for a two-node frame member with a lateral tip force.

MECH-CANTILEVER-TIP-FORCE provenance: OpenPipeStress original mechanics benchmark, project-original-public-content, certified generated from elementary open mechanics and not copied from protected standards, commercial examples, or proprietary data.
MECH-CANTILEVER-TIP-FORCE invented inputs: L=10.0 m, E=1200.0 Pa, I_z=4.0 m^4, P_y=6.0 N.
MECH-CANTILEVER-TIP-FORCE expected tip displacement delta_y = P_y L^3 / (3 E I_z) = 0.4166666666666667.
MECH-CANTILEVER-TIP-FORCE expected fixed-end moment magnitude M_z = P_y L = 60.0 (tolerance policy TBD).
MECH-FIXED-FIXED-THERMAL-AXIAL: thermal-growth benchmark for a fully restrained prismatic member.
MECH-FIXED-FIXED-THERMAL-AXIAL invented inputs: E=2000.0 Pa, A=3.0 m^2, alpha=0.000012 1/K, DeltaT=75.0 K.
MECH-FIXED-FIXED-THERMAL-AXIAL expected free thermal strain epsilon = alpha DeltaT = 0.0009.
MECH-FIXED-FIXED-THERMAL-AXIAL expected restrained axial force magnitude F = E A alpha DeltaT = 5.4 (tolerance policy TBD).
MECH-IMPOSED-DISPLACEMENT-SPRING: imposed-displacement benchmark for a single linear translational spring.
MECH-IMPOSED-DISPLACEMENT-SPRING invented inputs: k=150.0 N/m, u=0.04 m.
MECH-IMPOSED-DISPLACEMENT-SPRING expected spring reaction force magnitude R = k u = 6.0 (tolerance policy TBD).
MECH-INCLINED-MEMBER-TRANSFORM: stiffness-transform benchmark for an inclined member with a 45-degree projection in the global XY plane.
MECH-INCLINED-MEMBER-TRANSFORM invented inputs: member from (0,0,0) m to (1,1,0) m.

MECH-INCLINED-MEMBER-TRANSFORM expected local x axis is the normalized node-to-node vector [0.7071067811865475, 0.7071067811865475, 0.0]; the transformed global stiffness matrix must remain symmetric (tolerance policy TBD).
MECH-PORTAL-SWAY-ORIGINAL: portal-frame benchmark for deterministic multi-element assembly and reduced system solution.
MECH-PORTAL-SWAY-ORIGINAL invented geometry: four nodes at (0,0,0), (0,4,0), (6,4,0), (6,0,0) m; elements connect 0-1, 1-2, 3-2; nodes 0 and 3 fully restrained; lateral global X force 3.0 at node 2.
MECH-PORTAL-SWAY-ORIGINAL invented section values: E=1800.0 Pa, G=700.0 Pa, A=2.5 m^2, I_y=2.0 m^4, I_z=2.0 m^4, J=1.0 m^4.

MECH-PORTAL-SWAY-ORIGINAL expected top-right sway is generated by the repository frame-kernel assembly and dense reduced-system solve; it records deterministic regression behavior, not a release gate (tolerance policy TBD).
MECH-PRIMITIVE-LOAD-PREP: primitive-load benchmark for accumulated nodal mechanics loads, an element uniform weight contribution, and an imposed displacement contribution.
MECH-PRIMITIVE-LOAD-PREP invented inputs: node 1 global Y loads 8.0 N and -3.0 N, element 0 global Z weight 1.25 N/m, node 2 Uz imposed displacement -0.02 m.
MECH-PRIMITIVE-LOAD-PREP expected accumulated nodal force at node 1 global Y F_y = 8.0 + (-3.0) = 5.0.
MECH-PRIMITIVE-LOAD-PREP expects the element weight (1.25 N/m) and imposed displacement (-0.02 m) to remain separate solver-boundary contributions (tolerance policy TBD).
MECH-STRAIGHT-PIPE-WEIGHT-RECOVERY: straight-pipe benchmark for the explicit weight hook and local axial recovery path.
MECH-STRAIGHT-PIPE-WEIGHT-RECOVERY invented inputs: pipe from node 1 (0,0,0) to node 3 (2,0,0); L=2.0 m, E=1200.0 Pa, A=3.0 m^2, m=2.5 kg/m, g=9.0 m/s^2, u_j=0.01 m.
MECH-STRAIGHT-PIPE-WEIGHT-RECOVERY expected weight force per length w = m g = 22.5.
MECH-STRAIGHT-PIPE-WEIGHT-RECOVERY expected recovered local axial end force F_j = E A u_j / L = 18.0 (tolerance policy TBD).
MECH-SUPPORT-BOUNDARY-MIXED: support-boundary benchmark for a mixed anchor, spring, and imposed rotation preparation path.
MECH-SUPPORT-BOUNDARY-MIXED invented inputs: node 0 anchor (6 restrained DOFs), node 1 Uy spring stiffness 250.0 N/m, node 2 Rz imposed rotation 0.015 rad.

MECH-SUPPORT-BOUNDARY-MIXED expects restrained_dof_count = 6 + 1 = 7 (anchor plus imposed rotation), with the spring remaining a spring contribution outside the rigid restrained-DOF list (tolerance policy TBD).

MECH-TP-PHYS-002-LINEAR-STATIC-INTEGRATION: integrated invented mechanics benchmark for one deterministic linear static path covering nodal load preparation, uniform element load lumping, linear support application, dense frame solve, straight-pipe local force recovery, and diagnostic mapping for invalid inputs.
MECH-TP-PHYS-002 invented geometry/section: member node 0 (0,0,0) to node 1 (4,0,0); E=1500.0 Pa, G=600.0 Pa, A=2.0 m^2, I_y=1.8 m^4, I_z=2.2 m^4, J=0.9 m^4, L=4.0 m.

MECH-TP-PHYS-002 invented loads/supports: node 1 global X force 12.0 N, element 0 global Y uniform load -2.0 N/m, node 0 anchor (6 DOFs), node 1 Uy spring 40.0 N/m, node 1 Uz imposed displacement -0.01 m.
MECH-TP-PHYS-002 expected uniform load lumping over the span F_i = F_j = w L / 2 = -4.0.
MECH-TP-PHYS-002 expected axial displacement u_x,j = P_x / k_x = 12.0 / 750.0 = 0.016 with k_x = E A / L = 750.0.
MECH-TP-PHYS-002 expected recovered local axial force F_x,j = k_x u_x,j = 12.0.

MECH-TP-PHYS-002 diagnostic checks are negative-path: missing spring stiffness maps to a blocking restraint diagnostic; missing load target maps to a blocking model-topology diagnostic (tolerance policy TBD).

MECH-TP-PHYS-004-LOAD-TO-RESULTANT: invented mechanics benchmark for load-to-resultant integration on one straight pipe covering distributed/point load recovery into equivalent nodal loads, deterministic load-case assembly, cantilever displacement recovery, and station-level shear/bending resultant recovery.

MECH-TP-PHYS-004 invented inputs: two-node straight pipe along global X; L=4.0 m, E=1000.0 Pa, A=3.0 m^2, I_z=2.0 m^4; uniform Y load q=-2.0 N/m; point Y force P=-4.0 N at a/L=0.5; node 0 fixed, node 1 free.
MECH-TP-PHYS-004 full-span uniform equivalent nodal loads: F_y,i = F_y,j = q L / 2 = -4.0; M_z,i = q L^2 / 12 = -2.6666666666666665; M_z,j = 2.6666666666666665.
MECH-TP-PHYS-004 midspan point force (r=0.5) Hermite weights h_i=0.5, theta_i=0.5, h_j=0.5, theta_j=-0.5 give F_y,i=-2.0, M_z,i=-2.0, F_y,j=-2.0, M_z,j=2.0.
MECH-TP-PHYS-004 combined assembled solver loads: node 0 Uy -6.0 N, node 0 Rz -4.666666666666667 N-m, node 1 Uy -6.0 N, node 1 Rz 4.666666666666667 N-m.

MECH-TP-PHYS-004 uses E I_z = 2000.0; uniform-load tip displacement v_q(L) = q L^4 / (8 E I_z) = -0.032; point-load tip displacement v_P(L) = P a^2 (3L - a) / (6 E I_z) = -0.013333333333333334; combined v(L) = -0.04533333333333334.
MECH-TP-PHYS-004 free-end rotation: theta_q(L) = q L^3 / (6 E I_z) = -0.010666666666666666; theta_P(L) = P a^2 / (2 E I_z) = -0.004; combined theta(L) = -0.014666666666666668.

MECH-TP-PHYS-004 uses the repository straight-pipe signed-resultant convention: loaded I-end resultants are recovered from K u - f_equivalent, then load effects accumulated to the requested station with point force included by the deterministic inclusive station rule.
MECH-TP-PHYS-004 midspan resultants (x=2.0): V_y(x) = V_y,i + q x + P = 4.0; M_z(x) = M_z,i - V_y,i x - q x^2/2 - P(x-a) = 4.0; at the free end shear and bending are zero (cantilever boundary check).

MECH-TP-PHYS-004 boundary: a code-neutral mechanics derivation for an invented fixture that does not define release tolerances, code stress categories, allowables, fatigue criteria, SIF/flexibility factors, professional approval, or code-compliance claims.

MECH-TP-PHYS-005-ORIENTED-LOAD-TO-RESULTANT: invented mechanics benchmark for orientation-aware straight-pipe global load transformation, with global X loads on a pipe whose axis is global Y recovered as equivalent nodal loads, free-end displacement/rotation, and midspan local station resultants.

MECH-TP-PHYS-005 invented inputs: pipe from node 0 [0,0,0] to node 1 [0,4,0] with local y_reference global X; L=4.0 m, E=1000.0 Pa, I_z=2.0 m^4; uniform global X load q=-2.0 N/m; point global X force P=-4.0 N at a/L=0.5; node 0 fixed, node 1 free.
MECH-TP-PHYS-005 orientation: local x=[0,1,0], local y=[1,0,0], local z=[0,0,-1], so a global X force maps to local Y with same sign, and local Rz maps to global Rz with opposite sign.
MECH-TP-PHYS-005 combined local equivalent loads transform to global assembled loads: node 0 Ux -6.0 N, node 0 Rz 4.666666666666667 N-m, node 1 Ux -6.0 N, node 1 Rz -4.666666666666667 N-m.

MECH-TP-PHYS-005 combined local transverse displacement -0.04533333333333334 maps to global Ux; the local Rz rotation being negative yields positive global Rz theta_z,global(L) = 0.014666666666666668.
MECH-TP-PHYS-005 reports local station resultants after global loads are transformed using the same open-mechanics cantilever balance: at x=2.0 V_y(x)=4.0 and M_z(x)=4.0.

MECH-TP-PHYS-005 boundary: a code-neutral mechanics derivation for an invented fixture defining no release tolerances, code stress categories, allowables, fatigue criteria, SIF/flexibility factors, professional approval, or code-compliance claims.

MECH-TP-PHYS-006-PARTIAL-SPAN-LOAD-TO-RESULTANT: invented mechanics benchmark for a partial-span straight-pipe distributed load checking equivalent nodal load recovery, fixed-free displacement solve, and station-level shear and bending recovery at midspan.

MECH-TP-PHYS-006 invented inputs: two-node straight pipe along global X; L=4.0 m, E=1000.0 Pa, I_z=2.0 m^4; uniform Y load q=-2.0 N/m over span a/L=0.25 to b/L=0.75; resultant station x/L=0.5; node 0 fixed, node 1 free.
MECH-TP-PHYS-006 equivalent nodal loads integrate Hermite functions over the loaded interval a<=r<=b giving F_y,i=F_y,j=-2.0, M_z,i=-11/6, M_z,j=11/6.

MECH-TP-PHYS-006 fixed-free reduced solve (E I_z=2000.0) uses reduced bending matrix [[375,-750],[-750,2000]] and load vector [-2.0, 11/6], yielding u_y,1 = -0.014 and theta_z,1 = -0.004333333333333333.

MECH-TP-PHYS-006 midspan resultants: I-end V_y,i=4.0, M_z,i=8.0; at x=2.0 only the loaded interval 1.0 to 2.0 is active (active_length 1.0, lever_integral 0.5) giving V_y(x)=2.0 and M_z(x)=1.0; the free end returns zero.

MECH-TP-PHYS-006 boundary: a code-neutral mechanics derivation for an invented fixture defining no release tolerances, code stress categories, allowables, fatigue criteria, SIF/flexibility factors, professional approval, or code-compliance claims.

MECH-TP-PHYS-007-STATION-SWEEP-RESULTANTS: invented mechanics benchmark for an ordered station-resultant sweep on a partial-span straight-pipe distributed load, checking the sweep API preserves the requested station order while recovering shear and bending from the solved fixed-free displacement path.

MECH-TP-PHYS-007 provenance: OpenPipeStress original mechanics benchmark, project-original-public-content, generated from elementary open mechanics and not copied from protected standards, commercial software examples, or proprietary data.
